title: Documentary Photography
description: The unflinching photograph — the FSA archive and the pioneers of the form.

items.title: Migrant Mother
items.description_narrative: This iconic photograph captures Florence Owens Thompson and her children, embodying the struggles of American migrant farmworkers during the Great Depression. The image powerfully conveys the destitution faced by many families during the 1930s.
items.tags: great depression, poverty, documentary photography, migrant, mother, 1930s, historical

items.title: The Steerage
items.description_narrative: Alfred Stieglitz's iconic photograph captures immigrants in the steerage section of a ship traveling from Europe to America, depicting the stark social realities of early 20th-century transatlantic journeys. Celebrated for its powerful geometric composition and use of light and shadow, the image became a pivotal work in modern photography.
items.tags: photography, immigration, modernism, social commentary, geometric composition, photo-secession, early 20th century

items.title: Power house mechanic working on steam pump
items.cultural_context: Social documentary photography, Early 20th Century American
items.description_narrative: This powerful photograph captures a lone mechanic, immersed in the intricate work of maintaining a large steam pump. Lewis Hine's lens elevates the labor of the industrial worker, emphasizing the skill and dedication essential to modern progress.
items.tags: labor, industry, worker, machinery, documentary photography, early 20th century, social realism

items.title: The Horse in Motion
items.cultural_context: Victorian era, American photography, scientific photography
items.description_narrative: This groundbreaking series of photographs captured a horse mid-gallop, definitively proving that all four hooves leave the ground simultaneously. It represents a pivotal early experiment in chronophotography, laying foundational groundwork for motion pictures.
items.tags: photography, chronophotography, motion study, animal study, science, horse, early cinema

items.title: Allie Mae Burroughs
items.description_narrative: This poignant portrait captures Allie Mae Burroughs, the wife of an Alabama sharecropper, with a direct and unvarnished gaze. Photographed by Walker Evans in 1936, it stands as an iconic image from his powerful documentation of rural life during the Great Depression.
items.tags: portrait, woman, alabama, documentary photography, realism, black and white, great depression

items.title: View from the Window at Le Gras
items.description_narrative: This landmark image, captured by Nicéphore Niépce, is widely recognized as the world's first successful permanent photograph created with a camera obscura. The heliograph depicts the view from a window at Niépce's estate in Saint-Loup-de-Varennes, France.
items.tags: photography, landscape, heliography, early photography, camera obscura, French, invention
